fields.name: sourceurl
fields.doc: Canonical URI of the source text object, filling `sourceurl` (65026).

fields.name: rownum
fields.doc: 1-based physical line number within the source object.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: UTC instant captured from the line header, at microsecond resolution. Capture context, and only that: it is the clock the bridge stamped the *line* with, so it dates no message and never reaches one. What dates a message is what the message states -- its `TransactTime`, else its `SendingTime`, else the one instant the codec is pinned with -- so the same bytes logged at three hops settle on one instant however each line was stamped.

fields.name: timepartition
fields.doc: Timestamp partitioned by its UTC hour in Iceberg. `logs.messages` is laid out by it and `fix.messages` carries it as an ordinary column: a settled message is laid out by the instant it happened at, not by the instant a bridge printed the line.

fields.name: threadId
fields.doc: Bridge thread identifier captured from the line header.

fields.name: msgsessionid
fields.doc: Bridge session instance the line was handled on, filling `msgsessionid` (65032). The session *instance*, which is the bracket's own first part -- never what the message says about the counterparty session it names. Two connections to one counterparty are two instances, so they are two facts, and the event's own capture record holds this one.

fields.name: msgseqnum
fields.doc: Bridge sequence number, filling `MsgSeqNum` (34) where a frame stated none.

fields.name: pluginid
fields.doc: Bridge plugin that wrote the line, filling `pluginid` (65009).

fields.name: level
fields.doc: Severity spelling captured from the line header.

fields.name: bodyhash
fields.doc: XXH3-128 digest of the exact *body* bytes, computed beside them on the read. The key of `logs.messages`, and a digest of the bytes alone: identical bytes are one row whatever session carried them, whichever object they were read from and however often a capture is re-read. It is not the message's `hashcode`, which covers the settled event -- its facts, its text, its metadata and its entry tree -- and answers the same code for two different lines that state the same message. The bytes and the message are two questions, so they are two columns and neither stands in for the other.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: Exact bytes after the matched line-header prefix. `logs.messages` is where they live and the only place: `fix.messages` references them by `bodyhash` rather than repeating them, because a row there is an event and these bytes are one line's.
